//: Composite and collection-group indexes Orbit needs.
Firestore auto-creates single-field indexes, but not these: a
collectionGroup query needs its scope declared explicitly, and any query
that filters on one field while ordering by another needs a composite.
You do not have to apply this file by hand. The first time each query
runs, Firestore fails with a console error containing a click-to-create
link that builds exactly the index below. This file exists so the set is
written down, reviewable, and deployable with:
firebase deploy --only firestore:indexes
Building an index over an empty collection is instant; over a large one
it can take minutes, during which the query keeps failing.

indexes.//: Home feed: newest posts across every community at once.
Which posts a given person has sparked, across all communities.
Which communities a given person belongs to.
Which events a given person has registered for.
A person's Locali-Tea votes and reactions, for restoring their own state.

//: 48-hour self-deletion for Locali-Tea. Postgres did this in SQL; here
it is a native TTL policy on expiresAt, which db.js stamps at write
time. Firestore sweeps expired documents within about 24 hours of the
timestamp, so fetchTea() ALSO filters on the client — a post is
invisible the moment it expires rather than whenever the sweeper next
runs. Both are needed: the filter for correctness, the TTL so the
collection does not grow without bound.
TTL cannot be set from this file. Turn it on at:
Firebase Console -> Firestore -> Time-to-live -> Create policy
Collection group: tea_posts     Timestamp field: expiresAt
